title: Kingdom of Brittany
capsule: The Kingdom of Brittany emerged when Nominoë, appointed Carolingian missus and then duke, broke from Frankish overlordship and defeated Charles the Bald at Ballon in 845, establishing effective Breton independence. His son Erispoë won formal royal recognition from Charles the Bald after the Battle of Jengland in 851, and his cousin and supplanter Salomon (r. 857–874) expanded the realm to its greatest extent, gaining the Cotentin and parts of Maine before his assassination by rebellious nobles in 874. The kingdom then fell into internal strife and mounting Viking raids that devastated the peninsula and drove its leaders into exile, dissolving effective royal Breton authority well before Norse occupation overran the region.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Breton territory is documented from Carolingian diplomas and annals; Salomon's maximal borders are partially reconstructed from narrative sources and carry moderate uncertainty.
